findings.reason: the section as written either needs the trust rule to survive a report that moves no recorded directory, or the acceptance to name the window it is measuring; as it stands a node implements to the letter and the gate it was accepted on fails at a cadence its own evidence documents.
findings.text: §15 trusts the detector's record only while "the tree's change generation is still the one that was current when that pass completed", and it names every kernel project watch report as a report that starts a new generation; its control in case (4) confirms the intent ("An invalidation from the kernel project watch that lands after the detector's last pass makes the next read stat every recorded directory"). The section does not exclude the traffic its own Why blames for the whole problem: crew writes under `docs/state/reckon` that hold no covered file, which the section says arrive "several times a minute" and §7's landed evidence measures as "invalidate it every few seconds". Each such report is consumed by the fleet watch's reader thread for every tree, bumps the generation, and leaves the record untrusted until the next stat-ing pass — at most one per `_CROSS_NODE_FAST_S` (10 s). So for the read that follows a crew write the section is back on the full ~2,500-directory stat sweep, which is exactly the 6.5 s cost §15 was written to remove, and the accepted measure ("The second pass, a read after detector passes have run, must answer in under 1 s") is left to land in the seconds between a pass and the next crew write rather than being produced by the mechanism

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_reuse_covered`, `covered_dir_identity` (metadata_index.py:168), `_dir_identity` (879), `_fast_tree` (change_streams.py:414), `_invalidate_tree_views` (serve.py:1443), `_covered_files_for_project` (801) and `build_index` (530) all resolve at the cited revisions; §15's "cost stays open, recorded with §7's evidence" resolves to the `id="s7"` record in `docs/evidence/archive/the-page-paints-from-an-index-landed.html`, which carries the failing table and closes "By this section's rule the repair becomes a new section".
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of the five cases carries its own control, the module-window test named for `reckon/serve.py` exists and its bound is real — serve.py is 167,680 bytes against a 50,000-token allowance at the repository's own 3.5 bytes/token estimate, so the constraint the plan names is checkable.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs go under the run directory with a revision header and a trailing `EXIT=`, and suites are named for the fleet allocation rather than the login node.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach the named test module or the symbols the section introduces, and the section states mechanisms rather than tracker history.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the trust rule the section rests on is invalidated by the same change cadence its own Why cites, so the mechanism does not reliably produce the second-pass gate the section accepts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s15 carries one deliverable (trust the detector's stat pass) and one measure, despite spanning three write paths.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s15 declares `depends-on` s14, which itself depends on s13, so the reuse path s15 builds on is reachable; no declared relationship points at a node that does not exist.
